rationale: Reproduces unchanged at 9d981e5e — no commit in d796bf7d..9d981e5e touches vendors/. Bucket and Region come straight out of the vendor's /getfileuploadtoken JSON (juniper.go: `Bucket: firstNonEmpty(env.Bucket1, env.Bucket2)`); the only gate before use is a non-empty check in the ordered missing-field loop. s3Endpoint then builds `host := t.Bucket + ".s3." + t.Region + ".amazonaws.com"` and RETURNS A CONCATENATED STRING (`u.Scheme + "://" + u.Host + "/" + s3EscapePath(...)`) — the url.URL value is never used to parse or validate, so its `if u.Host == ""` guard is dead (Host was just assigned a non-empty literal). A bucket of `evil.example/` or `x@evil.example` makes http.NewRequestWithContext parse the authority as the attacker's host; the request then carries the redacted-but-still-customer evidence bundle AND the STS credentials (X-Amz-Security-Token session token, the access key id inside Authorization) to that host. signV4 signs whatever req.URL.Host says, so nothing downstream notices. Cisco's cxdBase is the pattern that should have been copied: `if h := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(host)); h != "" && h != CXDHost { return "" }` with the caller refusing on empty. rc1_blocking: touches credentials/secrets egress and customer-data destination, even though it needs a hostile or compromised vendor response — the whole point of the pinning is that the vendor response is untrusted input (§3).
evidence: s3put.go:46 `host := t.Bucket + ".s3." + t.Region + ".amazonaws.com"` then `return u.Scheme + "://" + u.Host + "/" + s3EscapePath(t.ObjectKey), nil` — no charset check, no suffix pinning, and the url.URL is decorative. juniper.go:296-320 accepts Bucket/Region verbatim from the JSON envelope, validating only non-emptiness. cisco.go:107-117 cxdBase refuses any host but the pinned CXDHost. s3put_test.go only ever uses `examplebucket`/`us-east-1`, so no test exercises a hostile bucket.
suggested_fix: Validate Bucket and Region against a strict charset (bucket: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9.-]{1,62}$ with no consecutive dots; region: ^[a-z0-9-]{1,32}$) in GetFileUploadToken before the token is returned, refuse with ErrRequestInvalid naming the field, and additionally assert in s3Endpoint that the parsed request host ends in ".amazonaws.com" (parse with url.Parse and compare u.Host, do not re-concatenate).

rationale: Reproduces at 9d981e5e. The hand-rolled fetch sends only Authorization; every request() call and the sibling hand-rolled downloads that DO carry scope set `if (scope) headers["X-Acting-Tenant"] = scope`. Server side, /api/tac/learning/export runs through LearningAPI.scoped, which resolves the caller to one concrete tenant and refuses a cross principal with 400. Consequences, both real: (a) platform owner — cross by default, and with a tenant selected the header never arrives, so p.Cross stays true and the export is a permanent 400 while the candidate list beside it (which goes through request()) loads fine; (b) a multi-scope operator acting as tenant B gets tenant A's (their home tenant's) candidates in the exported YAML while the list on screen shows B's — a wrong-tenant artifact that is then hand-merged into the shipped catalogue. NOTE the finding's 'only hand-rolled fetch in the file that omits it' clause is WRONG — reportPreview (6013), downloadArtifact (6024), exportLogRows (6045) and exportLogQuery (6066) omit it too; that does not change this row's verdict but those are the same defect elsewhere and should be swept with it. rc1_blocking: customer-visible correctness plus tenant-scoping of a downloaded artifact.
evidence: api.ts:6913 `const res = await fetch(`/api/tac/learning/export?dialect=...`, { headers: { ...(token ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } : {}) } });` — no scope. Contrast tacDownloadBundle at 6683-6686: `const scope = getActiveScope(); if (scope) headers["X-Acting-Tenant"] = scope;`. learninghttp.go:117-129 scoped(): `t, err := concreteTenantID(p.Tenant); if err != nil || p.Cross { ... http.StatusBadRequest ... "select a tenant to review its TAC learning backlog" }`, and export() calls `a.scoped(w, r, TemplateGateRead)` at line 451.
suggested_fix: Add the same two lines the neighbouring downloads use (read getActiveScope(), set X-Acting-Tenant when non-empty), and sweep the other four hand-rolled fetches in the file for the same omission.

rationale: The core defect reproduces: the effect that clears tacCase/escalateOpen/irisOpen/handoffNote/laneStates is keyed on `corrId`, which is `""` for every described investigation, so investigation→investigation switches never run it. After escalating investigation A, `tacCase` survives the switch and `shownCase = tacCase ?? recordedCase` renders A's case number and vendor status under investigation B, which may have no case at all — a false claim that B is escalated. One part of the filed text is NOT reproducible and should be dropped from the fix scope: TacEscalationPanel is NOT stale — it has its own reset effect keyed on `[incidentId, readState]` that clears ~30 pieces of state and re-reads, so the escalation flow itself rebinds correctly; and the chip's Refresh posts to `api.tacCaseRefresh(picked.id)`, i.e. the NEW incident id, so it returns/records the correct case rather than mutating A's — the harm is the misleading pre-refresh chip, not a cross-case write. IrisLane also persists (caseId is `corrId || undefined` = undefined for both investigations), so a previous investigation's answer does stay on screen. rc1_blocking: customer-visible correctness — the UI asserts a vendor case exists for an incident that has none.
evidence: InvestigationPage.tsx:163 `const corrId = picked?.kind === "correlation" ? picked.id : "";` then :167-170 `setObj(null); ... setTacCase(null); if (!corrId) return;` with deps `[corrId]` at :180. Render at :354-359 `{shownCase && (<TacCaseChip link={shownCase} incidentId={picked.id} .../>)}` — stale link, new id. Refuting half: TacEscalationPanel.tsx:408-420 resets everything and `void readState();` with deps `[incidentId, readState]`.
suggested_fix: Key the reset effect on the picked identity, not on corrId (e.g. `[picked?.kind, picked?.id]`), or give the answer-card subtree a `key={picked.id}`; guard the corrId-only fetches inside with the existing `if (!corrId) return`.

rationale: Reproduces. `uploadToken` is declared (341), cleared in the incident reset (417) and after a confirm (564), and sent through buildConfirmRequest (556 → tacModel.ts:1295 `body.upload_token = ...`), but grep over the whole tree finds NO setUploadToken call other than those two clears — no input, no paste box, nothing in ConnectorSettings/TicketDelivery either. The confirmation screen renders a 'Case number' box under needsExistingCase but nothing for the token. Server side that makes cisco-cxd permanently unusable from the UI: caseFormBaseValues maps `"upload_token": nonEmptyMark(req.Secrets.UploadToken)` and Prepare builds its CaseRequest with no Secrets, so the upload_token RequiredField is always in form.MissingRequired → `p.Blockers` → `p.Ready = len(p.Blockers) == 0 && ...` is false → the Confirm button is `disabled={!proposal.ready ...}`. The blocker's settings_hint is `fromSCM = "the case form (copy it from Cisco Support Case Manager)"`, which matches none of SETTINGS_ROUTES, so settingsHref returns "" and it renders as an inert `<span className="fact-line">` pointing the operator at a field that does not exist. This is a defect against stated behaviour, not a plain FEATURE_GAP: the code comment at 339 says 'It is typed here, sent once and never stored', the required-field Why says the operator supplies it per attach, and caseconn_probe.go says 'CXD stores no credential ... supplied when you attach'. rc1_blocking: customer-visible correctness — a shipped Tier-2 vendor route cannot complete and the UI instructs an impossible action.
evidence: Only three hits for the setter: `const [uploadToken, setUploadToken] = useState("")` (341), `setUploadToken(""); setUploadHost("");` (417) and (564). caseconn_required.go:153 `{Key: "upload_token", Label: "the per-case CXD upload token", SettingsHint: fromSCM, ...}` with fromSCM defined at :92 as 'the case form (copy it from Cisco Support Case Manager)'; tacModel.ts:1310-1327 SETTINGS_ROUTES has no key matching that string, so settingsHref → "". escalate.go:441 `p.Ready = len(p.Blockers) == 0 && (route.Portal || info.Configured)`; caseconn_tac.go:407 `"upload_token": nonEmptyMark(req.Secrets.UploadToken)` with Prepare's caseReq (escalate.go:417-421) carrying no Secrets.
suggested_fix: Render a password-type token input (and optional host) on the confirmation screen whenever the proposal carries an `upload_token` blocker — same treatment as the existing_case_number box — and either map fromSCM to no-link deliberately or reword the hint to name the on-screen field.

rationale: Reproduces. The page loads exactly one page — `api.ticketsOutbox(PAGE, 0)` with PAGE = 50, offset 0 — and the Queued/Failed/Delivered stat strip is computed by looping that array. Both stores return the OLDEST rows first (MemStore sorts `out[i].CreatedAt.Before(out[j].CreatedAt)`; PGStore `ORDER BY created_at LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2`) and nothing prunes ticket_outbox (no DELETE FROM ticket_outbox anywhere; the only delete is the dead-letter revive in EnqueueOutbox). So once a tenant has more than 50 outbox rows the three headline numbers freeze on the first 50 rows ever written and never again reflect a new failure: 'Failed 0' while deliveries are dead-lettering. The 'Showing the first N of M rows' caveat exists but sits under the Outbox table heading (line 325) and says nothing about the stat strip above it, which reads as a live health summary. rc1_blocking: silent failure of the operator surface whose job is to report delivery failure.
evidence: TicketDelivery.tsx:50 `const PAGE = 50;`; :126 `const r = await api.ticketsOutbox(PAGE, 0);`; :217-220 `for (const r of outbox ?? []) c[laneOf(r.status)] += 1;` feeding `<Stat label="Failed" value={counts.failed} tone={counts.failed > 0 ? "bad" : ""} />`. store.go:346 `sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].CreatedAt.Before(out[j].CreatedAt) })`; store.go:736 `SELECT ... FROM ticket_outbox ORDER BY created_at LIMIT $1 OFFSET $2`.
suggested_fix: Count server-side — return per-status totals from /api/tickets/outbox (a GROUP BY status alongside the count(*)) and render those — or at minimum page newest-first and label the strip as a sample. Server-side counts are the only version that stays true as the outbox grows.

rationale: Reproduces exactly as filed. ReviewRegistry.rows is keyed by the bare device key (`planDeviceKey` → DeviceID or Hostname, no tenant, no incident) and Register REPLACES the entry with no refcount; Release deletes it outright from runCollect's defer. The busy check in StartCollect is per-incident (`st.Job`), so two escalations on two different incidents naming the same device both reach Register; the second overwrites the first's set, then the Collector's own per-device claim (`if !c.claim(key) { return nil, ErrCollectBusy }`) refuses it, runCollect returns and its `defer s.reviews.Release(planDeviceKey(plan))` deletes the entry while collection #1 is still running — from that instant Gate.Allows falls through to `if g.reviews == nil || !g.reviews.allows(reviewKey(dev), command) { return false }` and every remaining reviewed/custom command in the live collection is refused. It fails CLOSED and the refusal is recorded on the capture row, so it is degraded evidence, not a widened attack surface: even in the overlap window the borrowed set only ever admits strings that some operator validated, and the running plan can only issue its own commands. rc1_blocking false on that basis — no isolation, privilege, data-loss or silent-failure consequence, and the operator sees the refusals. Worth fixing because the failure is invisible in the moment and lands in an evidence bundle a TAC engineer reads.
evidence: service.go:501 `s.reviews.Register(planDeviceKey(plan), commandsOf(plan))`; templates.go:718-722 `r.mu.Lock(); defer r.mu.Unlock(); r.rows[deviceKey] = set` (replace, no count) and :727-732 `delete(r.rows, deviceKey)`; service.go:544 `defer s.reviews.Release(planDeviceKey(plan))`; collect.go:352 `if !c.claim(key) { return nil, ErrCollectBusy }`. service.go:470 shows the busy guard is per-incident state (`if st.Job != nil && st.Job.Status == JobRunning`), so a second incident on the same device passes it.
suggested_fix: Key the registry by device key + a per-collection token (the job id) and have Release take the same token so a stale releaser is a no-op, or refcount the entry; the cheapest correct form is `rows map[string]map[string]bool` keyed by `deviceKey+"\x00"+jobID` with Gate.Allows consulting the claim's current job.

rationale: Reproduces. Confirm's only precondition is `st == nil || st.Proposal == nil`; it then reads `capture := st.Capture` and only fills the device identity `if capture != nil`. StartCollect sets `st.Capture = nil` (after Close) and never touches st.Proposal, so the sequence prepare → start a second collection → Confirm submits a CaseRequest with DeviceID/Hostname/Platform empty and ClassID left at the fallback `p.Form.ConnectorID` (a connector slug where a class id belongs). The vendor artefact is then wrong at the seam: portaltext.go:156 prints `DEVICE:  ()` and caseconn_tac.go:713 sends `DeviceID: orDefault(req.Hostname, req.DeviceID)` = empty into the real Cisco/Juniper case request, while the prepared form's title/description still describe the device from the discarded capture — and the attached bundle is the pre-existing one, not the collection now running. Raising rc1_blocking above the filed 'low' consequence: this produces an externally submitted, irreversible vendor case that names no device, with no signal to the operator (Confirm succeeds).
evidence: escalate.go:548-552 `if st == nil || st.Proposal == nil { ... }` — the only guard; :554-555 `p := st.Proposal; capture := st.Capture`; :566-573 `req := CaseRequest{... ClassID: p.Form.ConnectorID ...}; if capture != nil { req.ClassID = capture.ClassID; req.DeviceID, req.Hostname, req.Platform = capture.DeviceID, capture.Hostname, capture.Platform }`. service.go:481-483 `if err := st.Capture.Close(); err != nil {...}; st.Capture = nil` with no `st.Proposal = nil` beside it. portaltext.go:156 `fmt.Fprintf(&b, "DEVICE: %s (%s)\n", firstNonEmpty(req.Hostname, req.DeviceID), req.Platform)`.
suggested_fix: Invalidate the proposal wherever the capture it was built from is dropped (`st.Proposal = nil; st.Route = nil` in StartCollect, so the screen re-prepares), and make Confirm refuse when the proposal's capture is gone rather than submitting a device-less request — the fallback `ClassID: p.Form.ConnectorID` should go with it.

where: src/backend/internal/tac/service.go:609-624 (Bundle) + collect.go:170-180 (Capture.Close) + bundle.go:374-382 (BuildBundle reads SpillPath) + service.go:411-418 (dropLocked) and service.go:481-490 (StartCollect)
rationale: Reproduces at 9d981e5e; untouched by any commit in d796bf7d..9d981e5e (only cae55c51 and a097316d touched internal/tac, both in ticketing/cisco territory). Service.Bundle takes s.mu, copies the *Capture pointer into in.Capture, then UNLOCKS before calling BuildBundle. BuildBundle iterates in.Capture.Commands and reads cc.SpillPath; Capture.Close() concurrently writes c.Commands[i].SpillPath = "" and os.RemoveAll(dir) on the same slice, from three unlocked-relative-to-Bundle call sites: StartCollect (service.go:485), runCollect's completion (service.go:586) and dropLocked (service.go:415), the last reachable whenever any caller creates a 65th escalation state for the tenant (evictLocked -> dropLocked, which skips only RUNNING jobs — a bundle build is not a Job). Two consequences, both real: (a) a plain Go data race on Commands[i].SpillPath, which the CI -race gate would flag; (b) evidence loss — if the blank lands before BuildBundle reads the entry, bundle.go takes the else branch and writes renderOutput(cc), and a streamed command's Output field is empty by construction (collect.go:77 'Output is EMPTY for a STREAMED command; its body is in SpillPath'), so the vendor gets a header-only stub where the tech-support file should be, and bundleFile.sum() hashes that stub into SHA256SUMS as if it were the real body. If the directory is removed but SpillPath survives, writeTo's os.Open failure path at least says so in the file; the blanked-path variant says nothing at all. rc1_blocking: durable evidence loss in a customer-facing artifact plus a silent (unreported) substitution, plus a race.
evidence: service.go: `in.Capture = st.Capture` … `s.mu.Unlock()` … `b, err := BuildBundle(ctx, in, s.narrator, s.now)` — the pointer escapes the lock. collect.go:170 `func (c *Capture) Close() error { … for i := range c.Commands { c.Commands[i].SpillPath = "" } ; return os.RemoveAll(dir) }`. bundle.go:377 `if cc.SpillPath != "" { f.head = …; f.path = cc.SpillPath } else { f.data = []byte(renderOutput(cc)) }`.
suggested_fix: Either hold a refcount/lease on the Capture across BuildBundle (Close defers until the last reader drops it), or deep-copy the Commands slice (paths included) under the lock and pin the spill dir for the duration of the build. Do not simply hold s.mu across BuildBundle — that serialises every escalation on a multi-MB zip.

where: src/backend/internal/tac/escalatehttp.go:584 (HandleClassify) and :613 (HandlePlan); gate at src/backend/protocol_diagnostics.go tacEscalateSubject/tacResolveIncident; roles at src/backend/internal/rbac/roles.go:182,211
rationale: Reproduces. Resolve(w,r,false) maps to LevelRead via tacEscalateSubject (`level := LevelRead; if write { level = LevelWrite }`), and the built-in Read-only role holds infrastructure at LevelRead (roles.go:182 `readonly := all(LevelRead)`), so RoleReadOnly ('View everything, change nothing.') can POST both routes. Both routes MUTATE server-side state: Classify writes st.Classification and NULLS a plan built for the old class (`if st.Plan != nil && st.Plan.ClassID != res.ClassID { st.Plan = nil }`), Plan overwrites st.Plan. Worse, both go through stateLocked, which for an incident not yet in the register calls evictLocked; at maxEscalationsPerTenant that calls dropLocked, which calls st.Capture.Close() → os.RemoveAll of another operator's spill directory. So a read-only principal can destroy collected device evidence. I considered INTENTIONAL: the read gate has been there since the feature landed (d94a871d used LevelRead for classify/plan from day one, LevelWrite for collect/case), and the design intent is plausibly 'thinking, not touching a device'. But nothing states it — every other mutating handler in this file carries the write flag with an explicit reason (HandleCollect: '// A collection operates against a device → write level.'), and no comment, doc or test sanctions a read-only principal mutating shared state or triggering eviction. That is a privilege boundary, so it does not qualify as INTENTIONAL on the evidence available. Note for the fixer: HandleRefresh (escalatehttp.go:469) is on the same read gate and makes an outbound vendor call plus a PersistCase write; it was not filed but sits in the same class.
evidence: escalatehttp.go:584 and :613 `subj, ok := a.deps.Resolve(w, r, false)`; contrast :701 `// A collection operates against a device → write level.` / `Resolve(w, r, true)`. protocol_diagnostics.go tacEscalateSubject: `level := LevelRead; if write { level = LevelWrite }`; tacResolveIncident: `claims, ok := s.requirePerm(w, r, "infrastructure", level)`. service.go:411 dropLocked: `if err := st.Capture.Close(); err != nil { s.warn("an evicted TAC capture's streamed outputs could not be removed" …`.
suggested_fix: Move HandleClassify and HandlePlan to Resolve(w,r,true) with the same one-line reason comment HandleCollect carries. If read-only preview of a plan is genuinely wanted, split it into a non-recording dry preview and keep the recording variant at write level.

where: src/backend/internal/tac/plan.go:336-344 (the dead `if !seen[intent]` inside addBound), guard set at plan.go:310
rationale: Reproduces by inspection and is unambiguous. addBound sets seen[intent] = true on its third line, before the probe check; the probe branch then guards its Unbound append with `if !seen[intent]`, which can never be true at that point. Result: an intent whose dialect binding is a probe that did not render a destination is appended to NEITHER p.Steps NOR p.Unbound — it vanishes. The coverage sentence is then computed from those two slices, so if the dropped intent was the only one that would have been unbound, `len(p.Unbound) == 0` holds and the plan asserts 'Every command this class needs is authored for <dialect>.' That is a false coverage claim to the operator and a silently missing capture in the resulting bundle — silent failure plus customer-visible correctness, hence rc1_blocking. Reachable from shipped data, not just hypothetically: cisco-iosxe.yaml binds `ping {peer}` at lines 1576/1618/1624 (also `ping {peer} size 1500 df-bit` and `ping {vrf-scope} {prefix}`), cisco-iosxr.yaml at 1351; renderCommand DROPS an argument that does not match the argument shape ('An argument that does not match the narrow argument shape is DROPPED'), so an incident with no peer renders bare `ping`, IsProbeCommand returns true (lead token in probeLead) and ValidateBoundedProbe refuses it for having no destination. No test covers this path: grepping the exact reason string 'this dialect binds a reachability probe for it, but the incident supplied no address to probe' returns only plan.go:341 — the message it is supposed to emit is never asserted anywhere.
evidence: plan.go:308-311 `addBound := func(intent string, sec Section, b Binding) { if seen[intent] { return }; seen[intent] = true;` … plan.go:336-344 `if protocoldiag.IsProbeCommand(cmd) && protocoldiag.ValidateBoundedProbe(cmd) != nil { if !seen[intent] { seen[intent] = true; p.Unbound = append(...) } ; return }`. plan.go:441 `case len(p.Unbound) == 0: p.Note = "Every command this class needs is authored for " + dp.Display + "."`.
suggested_fix: Hoist the probe check above `seen[intent] = true`, or drop the inner guard entirely (the outer `if seen[intent] { return }` already makes it single-entry). Add a plan test that a class binding `ping {peer}` with an empty Target yields exactly one Unbound step carrying that reason and no coverage claim.

where: src/backend/internal/tac/yamlmin.go:275-286 (parseBlockScalar), reached from captureparse.go:322 parseCaptureYAML → captureshttp.go:289 ParseCapture on the capture-upload route
rationale:
REPRODUCED at 9d981e5e with a throwaway probe test in internal/tac (removed afterwards; no file left behind): input "name: x
note: |
      deep
    shallow
" panics with strings.Repeat negative count at yamlmin.go:282. `base` is fixed from the FIRST body line and never re-floored, so any later body line that is still deeper than the key's indent but shallower than the first body line yields a negative repeat count. Reachable from the authenticated customer capture-upload route (a.scoped(w,r,TemplateGateWrite) → infrastructure:write) — untrusted file content, bounded to 1 MiB but not otherwise shaped before parsing. There is no panic-recovery middleware in the api (grep for recover() across src/backend outside vendor/ finds only safego, protocoldiag/fanout and dataprotect/ops — none wrapping HTTP handlers), so containment is entirely net/http's per-connection recover: the process survives, the client gets a dropped connection instead of the 400 every other malformed upload gets, and the log takes a full stack trace per attempt. Kept at medium rather than raised, because it is not process death and the caller must already hold infrastructure:write; kept at medium rather than lowered, because it is an unhandled panic on attacker-supplied input in a shipped parser with a one-line fix, and rc1's list names 'process crash or panic' explicitly. The same parser also loads the shipped ai/tac catalogue at boot (load.go:76,379, forbidden.go:132) — those inputs are ours, so that is not the exposure, but a malformed shipped file would panic the boot rather than report a line number, which is the opposite of this file's stated contract ('REFUSED with the line number').
evidence: yamlmin.go:275-286 `base := -1; for len(lines) > 0 && lines[0].indent > indent { if base < 0 { base = lines[0].indent }; pad := strings.Repeat(" ", lines[0].indent-base); … }`. Probe run output: `strings.Repeat(...)` → `netops/backend/internal/tac.parseBlockScalar(...) yamlmin.go:282` → parseValue:254 → parseMap:162 → parseBlock:138 → parseYAML:81, FAIL netops/backend/internal/tac.
suggested_fix: Re-floor the base (`if lines[0].indent < base { base = lines[0].indent }`) or, better for this parser's stated contract, refuse a body line shallower than the first with a line-numbered error — a dedent inside a block scalar is malformed YAML and should be reported, not padded. Add the fixture to yamlmin_test.go.

where: src/backend/internal/ticketing/caseconn_tac.go:597-610 (attachOnlyMissingFields), enforced at :528 (SubmitCase) and :437 (missing-field report) and :117-128 (dry run); table at caseconn_required.go:139-144; email caps at attach_email.go:301
rationale: Reproduces. attachOnlyMissingFields unconditionally demands req.Secrets.UploadToken for EVERY connector whose Caps.AttachToExistingOnly is true. Two connectors set it: cisco-cxd (constant true, correct — CXD uses the token as the Basic-auth password) and email-cisco, where it is derived (`AttachToExistingOnly: c.vendor.Mode == EmailModeAttachOnly`, and attach_email.go:125 registers attach@cisco.com in EmailModeAttachOnly). The email transport never reads an upload token: EmailCaseConnector.AttachBundle builds the message from cfg.Email and ref.Number only, and touches no field of CaseRef other than Number/ID. So SubmitCase on email-cisco always returns tac.ErrFormIncomplete naming 'upload_token (the per-case credential from the vendor's portal)' — a credential Cisco does not issue for the attach mailbox and the operator therefore cannot supply. rationale: Both halves reproduce; nothing in d796bf7d..9d981e5e touches mailbox_send.go. rationale: Reproduces at 9d981e5e; learningstore.go is untouched since d796bf7d. `before := b.Records` saves a slice HEADER, then `append` writes into the same backing array whenever cap > len, and `sortRecords` (sort.SliceStable at :343) permutes that array IN PLACE. The cap>len precondition is guaranteed once a tenant reaches the ceiling: line 197-200 re-slices `b.Records = b.Records[:MaxRecordsPerTenant]` from a length-201 slice, leaving cap ≥ 201 > len 200 for every subsequent PutRecord. The in-memory view then disagrees with the file, and the next successful flush serialises the corrupted view and makes the loss permanent — the exact shape cb406a95/33303ace fixed for pcap and configstore ('a prune whose flush fails no longer loses the rows it kept … the rows were already gone from memory, it silently disagreed with the disk, and the next successful write … made the loss permanent'). rationale: The rollback is not a rollback. `prev := s.changes[t]` captures len=n over a backing array that almost always has spare capacity (each successful RecordChange assigns the result of `append`, which over-allocates, so cap>len on the following call). `append(prev, in)` then writes `in` at index n of THAT SAME array, and `trimChanges` sorts the whole n+1 slice IN PLACE. Because a newly recorded change is normally the newest, the sort moves `in` to index 0 and pushes the oldest element out to index n — outside prev's window. Restoring `s.changes[t] = prev` therefore restores a slice of the right LENGTH but the wrong CONTENTS: it contains the change the caller was just told failed, and has silently dropped the oldest retained change. The next successful RecordChange flushes that state to disk, so the loss becomes durable and the phantom row becomes persisted despite the producer having received a 500 (and having likely retried, minting a second id for the same event, since RecordChange mints the id when it is empty). Reachable on any flush failure (ENOSPC, EACCES, EIO) — exactly the condition the rollback exists for. Note this is the same defect family as the already-fixed cb406a95/33303ace/e8018b5f prune-rollback wave, but this call site was not touched.
evidence: store.go:352 `prev := s.changes[t]`; :360 `s.changes[t] = trimChanges(append(prev, in))`; :361-363 `if err := s.flushLocked(); err != nil { s.changes[t] = prev; return ChangeEvent{}, err }`; trimChanges at :465-473 is `sort.SliceStable(list, ...)` on the slice it was handed — an in-place sort of the array `prev` still points into. `git log d796bf7d..9d981e5e -- src/backend/internal/dem/` is EMPTY, so nothing in the 27-commit window touched this. No test asserts the rollback (store_test.go only covers RecordChange idempotency at :68/:75).
suggested_fix: Snapshot before mutating: `prev := append([]ChangeEvent(nil), s.changes[t]...)` (or build the new slice into a fresh backing array) so the rollback restores bytes nothing aliased.

rationale: Confirmed exactly as filed. The SQL pushes down only the time bound and the row cap; type/app/site are applied in Go afterwards over the already-truncated page. On a tenant with more than `limit` changes inside the lookback, `SELECT ... WHERE event_at >= $1 ORDER BY event_at DESC LIMIT $2` returns the newest 500 regardless of type, and the deploy the operator filtered for can sit at position 501 — the endpoint then prints "No change was recorded in this window" (http.go:1205) for a change that is in the table. The file backend calls filterChanges over the whole retained bucket and only then applies Limit, so the two backends answer differently for the same query. The columns needed to push the predicate down already exist (RecordChange inserts change_type, app, site as first-class columns), so this is not a schema limitation. Scope check: the RCA/assemble path (http.go:263) sets no type/app/site, so correlation input is unaffected — the damage is confined to the operator-facing change list, which is the "what changed" screen used during incident triage. rc1_blocking because a false "nothing changed" during triage is customer-visible correctness, and because the two backends disagree on the same API contract (PG is now the default backend for fresh installs, so the answer changes on the store cutover).

File twin, store.go:339: `return filterChanges(s.changes[t], q), nil` — filter first, `if q.Limit > 0 && len(out) > q.Limit { out = out[:q.Limit] }` last (store.go:459). suggested_fix: Add the type/app/site predicates to the WHERE clause (they are indexed columns already written by RecordChange) and keep filterChanges only as the shared post-check, so both backends bound the SAME set.

rationale: Confirmed on both stores. platformdb.Load is a bare os.ReadFile (kv.go:110), so it returns ENOENT, EACCES, EIO and EMFILE through the same error value; both NewFileStore functions treat every one of them as 'absent' and return an empty store WITHOUT setting loadErr. The wiring in probe_handlers.go only logs when LoadErr() is non-nil, so a read failure is completely silent — no log line, no metric, and the surface renders the honest-looking 'no journey is declared for this tenant' text. The first successful write then calls flushLocked → platformdb.Save → WriteFileAtomic, which renames a temp holding the EMPTY payload over the original, destroying every tenant's journeys, changes and promotions (or the whole target catalogue). It needs only a writable directory, which is the normal condition. Realistic triggers are not exotic: a data volume whose files carry a previous container UID, an fd-exhausted process at boot, or a transient EIO. The corrupt-JSON path is handled correctly by contrast (loadErr set, integrator logs it), which is what makes the read-error hole a genuine gap rather than a design choice — and the comment at dem/store.go:123 ("It is never silently overwritten either... the operator has been told why") is a claim this branch falsifies. Exposure is reduced but not removed by tracker 245 making Postgres the default for fresh installs: the file backend is the supported compat path and every pre-cutover install runs it.
evidence: experience/store.go:130-133 `b, err := platformdb.Load(path)` / `if err != nil { return s }` — no `s.loadErr = err`; dem/store.go:137-140 the same with the comment `return s // absent store → empty, not an error`. platformdb/kv.go:110 `func (f FileKV) Load(key string) ([]byte, error) { return os.ReadFile(f.resolve(key)) }` — every read error, not just fs.ErrNotExist. probe_handlers.go:101-105 and :513-518 log ONLY `if err := fs.LoadErr(); err != nil`, so this path emits nothing. Nothing in `git log d796bf7d..9d981e5e -- src/backend/internal/dem/` (empty) touched it.
suggested_fix: Branch on the error: `if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) { return s }` (genuinely absent) else `s.loadErr = err; return s` — and, for the write side, have flushLocked refuse to overwrite while loadErr is set, so an unreadable file is never replaced by an empty one.

rationale: Confirmed. JourneyForm seeds ALL of its state from `initial` in useState initialisers only (name, app, description, importance, value, currency, successPct, latencyMs, entry, steps) with no `key` on the element and no effect that resyncs when `initial` changes. React reconciles the same element type at the same position, so changing `editing` from journey A to journey B keeps the instance and every piece of A's state. The list panel is rendered ABOVE the form and its per-row Edit buttons and the 'Declare a journey' button stay live while the form is open, so the switch is a single click with nothing to warn the user. What ships afterwards is worse than a stale form: the Panel title reads from the fresh prop (`initial ? \`Edit ${initial.name}\``) so the header says 'Edit B', while the fields still hold A's name, SLO, business value and full step graph, and onSave is called with `editing.id` = B's id. Save therefore PUTs A's definition over B — B's step graph, objective and value are destroyed, and because the API is a full-document update there is nothing partial about it. The mirror case (Edit A → 'Declare a journey') creates a duplicate of A. This is operator-declared configuration that every downstream number is computed from (journey health, SLO miss, business impact, incident severity floor), so the corruption propagates into scoring and severity.
evidence: ExperienceJourneys.tsx:152-159 `{editing && (<JourneyForm initial={editing === "new" ? undefined : editing} ... onSave={(body) => save(body, editing === "new" ? undefined : editing.id)} />)}` — no key prop. Form state at :217-227 is all `useState(initial?.… ?? …)`; the only writes are the field onChange handlers, so nothing re-reads `initial` after mount. Title at :265 `<Panel title={initial ? \`Edit ${initial.name}\` : "Declare a journey"}` proves the prop DOES update while the state does not. The Edit button at :113 `onClick={() => setEditing(j)}` and the new button at :87 `onClick={() => setEditing("new")}` are never disabled while the form is open; `setEditing(null)` happens only on save success (:57) or cancel.
suggested_fix: Give the element an identity: `<JourneyForm key={editing === "new" ? "new" : editing.id} ... />` so switching targets remounts with the right seed.

rationale: Confirmed. The handler asks the store for at most maxPageLimit (500) rows and then derives every completeness signal from that already-truncated slice: `total: len(all)`, `X-Total-Count: len(all)` and `complete: httppage.Complete(page, len(rows), len(all))`, where Complete is `p.Offset == 0 && returned == total`. A caller that asks for limit=500 offset=0 on a tenant with more than 500 changes in the window is told returned==total, complete=true and X-Page-Done=true — the exact bit httppage documents as 'the one bit a client needs to tell a partial answer from a whole one'. The silence is doubled: LogTruncated returns early when Complete is true, so the operator-facing 'unpaged read truncated at the server ceiling' log never fires on precisely the case it was written for. On the PG backend it is worse than a miscount, because the store-level cap is applied BEFORE the type/app/site filter (see 3.2-03), so a filtered query can report a small honest-looking total with complete=true while most of the matching set was never examined. I have kept the filed severity at low — the headers still carry limit/max so a determined client can infer the ceiling, and the change list is advisory — but it is rc1_blocking: it is a false completeness claim on a customer-visible triage surface, in a codebase whose bounded-read contract exists specifically to never make that claim.
evidence: http.go:1188-1191 `cq := ChangeQuery{ ..., Limit: maxPageLimit }` with `maxPageLimit = 500` (http.go:59); :1196 `all, err := a.deps.Store.ListChanges(...)`; :1201-1203 `httppage.LogTruncated(ChangesPath, page, len(rows), len(all))` / `httppage.WriteHeaders(w, page, len(rows), len(all))`; :1210 `"complete": httppage.Complete(page, len(rows), len(all))`. httppage/page.go:194 `func Complete(p Request, returned, total int) bool { return p.Offset == 0 && returned == total }` and :50-53 `if p.Explicit || Complete(p, returned, total) { return }` in LogTruncated. Both backends cap at ChangeQuery.Limit (store.go:459, pg.go:229).
suggested_fix: Ask the store for limit+1 (or a real COUNT) and let the handler distinguish 'that is all of them' from 'that is all we would fetch': when the store returned its ceiling, report complete=false and let LogTruncated fire.

rationale: Reproduces unchanged at 9d981e5e (git diff d796bf7d..9d981e5e -- src/backend/internal/dem is empty). The GET arm collapses EVERY store error to 404: `def, err := a.deps.Store.GetJourney(...); if err != nil { http.NotFound(w, r) ... }`. PGStore.GetJourney distinguishes the two cases and returns them differently — pgx.ErrNoRows is converted to `ErrNotFound`, while any other `qerr` (connection refused, statement timeout under pgTimeout, RLS/SET failure inside WithTenant, json.Unmarshal of a corrupted blob) is returned verbatim — so a database outage or a corrupt row is rendered to the operator as 'this journey does not exist'. The PUT and DELETE arms in the same switch do it correctly (`if errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) { 404 } ... else 500`), which is proof of intent rather than a design choice. No log line and no counter fire on the path, so the misdiagnosis leaves no trace anywhere. rc1_blocking: silent failure + customer-visible correctness (a resource that exists is reported deleted, and the operator's next action after 'it's gone' is to recreate it). Severity stays low: read-only path, no write and no isolation consequence — the tenant scoping is still enforced by RLS/concreteTenant above the error branch.
evidence: http.go GET arm: `def, err := a.deps.Store.GetJourney(r.Context(), tenant, id)` / `if err != nil { http.NotFound(w, r) // cross-tenant id is indistinguishable from absent; return }`. pg.go:77-107 GetJourney: `if errors.Is(qerr, pgx.ErrNoRows) { return nil }` … `if qerr != nil { return qerr }` … `if !found { return JourneyDefinition{}, ErrNotFound }` — two distinct outcomes the handler merges. Contrast the DELETE arm: `if err := a.deps.Store.DeleteJourney(...); err != nil { if errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound) { http.NotFound(w,r); return }; a.deps.WriteError(w, http.StatusInternalServerError, err) }`.
suggested_fix: Mirror the DELETE arm: 404 only on errors.Is(err, ErrNotFound); anything else is a 500 through a.deps.WriteError plus a QueryErrors increment (see 3.2-12 — that counter currently reaches no surface, so the log line is the part that must land).

rationale: Same shape as 3.2-07 but a different package, a different handler and a different store — fixing one does not fix the other, so it is not filed as a duplicate. `t, err := a.deps.Targets.Get(r.Context(), tenant, id); if err != nil { http.NotFound(w, r) }` swallows every dem.PGStore.Get failure that is not pgx.ErrNoRows: the WithTenant/RLS setup, the pgTimeout deadline, and the json.Unmarshal of the stored row all return an error that becomes 'this target does not exist'. No log, no counter. rc1_blocking on silent failure and customer-visible correctness; severity stays low for the same reason as 3.2-07 (read path, no isolation or write consequence).

I RAISE low→medium on evidence the row does not carry: the router flattens these fields into ClickHouse columns declared `LowCardinality(String)` (deployment/docker/clickhouse/init.sql:1232-1238 and 1271-1277), and the producing credential is a GateIngest one the code itself says is a browser snippet, i.e. must be assumed public. Honest limit on the claim: the per-request caps (maxIngestBodyBytes 256 KiB, MaxEventsPerRequest 200) bound one request, so this is a per-value amplification, not an unbounded single request.

suggested_fix: Add a `func (c *Cohort) normalize()` that labelSafe/clips each of the eight dimensions and call it from ExperienceEvent.Validate, ExperienceSession.Validate, BusinessEvent.Validate and ChangeEvent.Validate — and either enforce MaxCohortDimensionsLen there or delete the constant so the next reader is not told a bound exists. Worth noting while in the file: the router maps only seven of the eight (cohort.feature_flag has no `.cohort_flag` line before `del(.cohort)` in vector.yaml:1005-1012), so that dimension is dropped in ClickHouse — related, out of this row's scope.

rationale: Reproduces, and the premise the row rests on is stronger than filed. The ClickHouse projection builds the grouping key with `concat(dst_addr, ':', toString(dst_port))` — no brackets around the address — and Go splits it with `strings.Cut(ep, ":")`, which cuts at the FIRST colon. For an IPv6 endpoint the row key is e.g. `2001:db8::1:443`, so addr becomes `2001` and portStr becomes `db8::1:443`; `strconv.Atoi` fails and the row is `continue`d. IPv6 subjects are reachable, not hypothetical: flowEndpointOf (experience/flow.go:277-290) accepts any literal `net.ParseIP` parses, explicitly strips `[]`, and stores `ip.String()`; ClickHouse `src_addr`/`dst_addr` are plain `String` (clickhouse/init.sql:27) and goflow2 decodes IPv6 NetFlow v9/IPFIX records. The SQL IN-list match therefore succeeds and the rows come back — every one of them is then discarded in the fold, silently: no counter, no log, and the subject simply produces no FlowStats, so the passive-flow anchor (the second anchor-capable evidence class, tracker 252) never fires for an IPv6-declared app. That is evidence loss that RCA reads as 'no flow record touched any declared subject', i.e. a wrong negative rather than an error. RAISED low→medium: total, silent loss of one evidence class for an entire address family, feeding correlation. rc1_blocking on RCA correctness + silent failure. The existing test is exactly the kind of double the brief warns about: TestFoldDEMFlowRowsAttributesOnlyDeclaredEndpoints uses only IPv4 keys and asserts that `"not-an-endpoint"` is dropped — an IPv6 key is well-formed but takes that same drop branch, and no test notices.
evidence: probe_handlers.go:266 `epExpr := "multiIf(dst_addr IN (" + in + "), concat(dst_addr, ':', toString(dst_port)), concat(src_addr, ':', toString(src_port)))"`; :301-309 `addr, portStr, found := strings.Cut(ep, ":")` / `if !found { continue }` / `port, perr := strconv.Atoi(portStr)` / `if perr != nil { continue }`. experience/flow.go:282-290 `host = strings.Trim(host, "[]"); ip := net.ParseIP(host); ...; return FlowEndpoint{Addr: ip.String(), Port: port}, true`. src/backend/dem_flow_isolation_test.go:139-165: every `ep` fixture is IPv4 (`10.1.0.1:443`, `10.1.0.9:53`, `10.9.9.9:443`, `not-an-endpoint`).
suggested_fix: Stop reconstructing a composite key: have the SQL select the endpoint address and port as two columns (`multiIf(...) AS ep_addr`, `multiIf(...) AS ep_port`) and read them separately, which removes the parse entirely. If the single key must stay, split on strings.LastIndex(ep, ":") — the canonical ip.String() form has no trailing brackets — and count a drop (`ep` unparseable) rather than a bare `continue`.

rationale: Reproduces. `Run` selects on ctx.Done() and returns immediately, leaving whatever is buffered in `q.ch` unsent, uncounted and unlogged. The contrast inside the same file is what makes this a defect rather than a shrug: `publish` drops loudly on purpose — it increments EventsDropped and logs 'those users' evidence is gone, not delayed' — and the ingest route's doc header states 'A 202 for data that went nowhere would make the lane look healthy while a tenant's evidence disappeared — the failure mode this whole product exists to refuse'. The shutdown path is precisely a 202 for data that went nowhere. The row's mitigation is accurate — main.go does httpSrv.Shutdown() before cancel(), so no new beacons arrive during the window — but it is not a bound on the loss: the channel holds DefaultQueueBatches (256) batches and MaxQueuedEvents is 20000, and the queue is only near-empty when the bus is healthy; a restart during a Kafka stall discards a full backlog with the lane's own dropped-events counter reading zero. Kept at low because the normal-path window is milliseconds and the events are already best-effort; rc1_blocking true on durable telemetry loss + silent failure, and because the fix is a bounded drain, not a redesign.
evidence: expbus.go Run: `for { select { case <-ctx.Done(): return; case b := <-q.ch: ... q.publish(ctx, b) } }` — no drain before the return, and no `q.metrics.EventsDropped.Add(len(q.ch)...)`. Compare publish's tail: `q.metrics.EventsDropped.Add(int64(b.events)); q.logWarn("experience events could not be published to the bus and were dropped — those users' evidence is gone, not delayed", ...)`. Wiring: main.go:2470 `workers.start("dem-experience-lane", func() { srv.experienceEvents.Run(ctx) })`, shutdown at main.go:2716-2720 `httpSrv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx)` then `cancel()`, then workers.drain(WORKER_DRAIN_TIMEOUT, default 15s) — so Run is already inside a waited drain and has a budget to spend.
suggested_fix: On ctx.Done, drain q.ch under a short deadline derived from the worker drain budget (publish with a fresh context.WithTimeout so the cancelled ctx does not abort each publish immediately), then account for whatever is still queued: EventsDropped.Add(remaining) plus one logWarn naming the count — the same treatment publish already gives an exhausted batch.

rationale: Both lenses reproduce. (a) Counters has 15 fields and Snapshot renders all 15, but metricHelp lists 9; Write iterates metricHelp, so events_ingested, business_ingested, ingest_refused, ingest_rejected, incidents_promoted and promotion_errors can never be emitted — the six added by the tracker-254/255 work, exactly the case the comment 'kept beside the counter so a new one cannot ship undocumented' was meant to prevent, and the invariant is already broken. (b) Nothing calls this Write at all: `srv.demExperienceMetrics = experience.NewCounters()` (main.go:1329) is handed to the API deps (probe_handlers.go:596) and read nowhere else; the /metrics assembly calls `s.demMetrics.Write(w)` (main.go:4411), which is the DIFFERENT `*dem.Metrics` built at main.go:1321. So the file's own doc claim — 'They are exposed on the platform's /metrics endpoint through the same Write hook internal/dem's counters use' — is false as written. rc1_blocking false, deliberately: no behaviour is wrong, no data is lost or leaked, and `grep -rn dem_experience src/config/*.yaml docs/runbooks src/frontend/src` returns nothing, so no alert rule, runbook or dashboard depends on these series — nothing regresses at rc1 and nothing that exists today goes dark. It is a missing observability surface, not a silent failure of a monitored path. It does, however, mean the counter half of the fixes for 3.2-07 and 3.2-08 would land nowhere, so this should be fixed first or those two should log rather than count. Severity stays low.
evidence: metrics.go: Counters has 15 atomic.Int64 fields; Snapshot returns 15 keys; metricHelp is a 9-entry `[][2]string`; `func (c *Counters) Write(w io.Writer) { ... for _, h := range metricHelp { fmt.Fprintf(w, ..., snap[h[0]]) } }` — the loop is over the help table, so an unlisted counter is unreachable. main.go:229 `demMetrics *dem.Metrics` vs :243 `demExperienceMetrics *experience.Counters`; the metrics handler writes only the former (`if s.demMetrics != nil { s.demMetrics.Write(w) }`). `grep -rn demExperienceMetrics src/backend --include=*.go` → main.go:243/1329, probe_handlers.go:596, and two tests; no /metrics call site. No dem_experience_* string anywhere in src/config, docs/runbooks or the frontend.
suggested_fix: Add the six missing HELP entries, and derive the rendering from Snapshot's keys (or add a table-driven test asserting len(metricHelp) == len(Snapshot()) so the stated invariant is mechanical rather than advisory). Then call `s.demExperienceMetrics.Write(w)` beside s.demMetrics in the /metrics assembly, or delete the block and the doc comment that claims it is exposed.

rationale: Reproduces exactly, and the impact is wider than filed. WireRun.Validate bounds ID/tenant/target/kind/vantage/outcome/retries and only checks `EndedAt` against `StartedAt` — there is no ceiling on StartedAt itself. pruneLocked keys retention off the NEWEST run in the ring (`ring[len(ring)-1].StartedAt`, the ring being sorted ascending), so one record dated in the future makes `Before(cutoff)`永 false and the ring is never dropped. Three consequences: (1) the ring permanently holds one of the platform-wide 5000 MaxTrackedDefinitions slots — `s.tracked` is a GLOBAL counter, not per tenant, so poisoned rings from one tenant/vantage eventually make `res.Dropped++` refuse NEW definitions for every other tenant, which is exactly the cross-tenant coupling the comment above that branch says it exists to prevent; (2) experience.GradeReliability applies no time window of its own (synthetic.go:264, it grades whatever list it is handed), so a check that has stopped running keeps grading `solid` forever off stale runs, and `Trustworthy` is what gates a high-severity experience incident — the stated invariant 'A target that stopped being measured stops being graded' is defeated; (3) the sibling ingest path already refuses exactly this input, so this is an inconsistency inside the same subsystem, not a missing feature. Realistic trigger is a skewed prober-container clock (the record's timestamps come from the prober host), not only a hostile writer; nothing self-heals it short of an api restart. Kept at low because it needs a bad clock or a writer on the KV channel, but rc1_blocking because it is durable state poisoning that produces a stale-good reliability grade (customer-visible / RCA-severity correctness) and a permanently consumed shared bound.
evidence: runs.go Validate: `if r.StartedAt.IsZero() { return errors.New("dem run: started_at is required") }` / `if !r.EndedAt.IsZero() && r.EndedAt.Before(r.StartedAt) {…}` — no upper bound anywhere. runs.go:268-275: `// pruneLocked drops rings whose newest run is older than RunRetention.` … `if len(ring) == 0 || ring[len(ring)-1].StartedAt.Before(cutoff) { delete(bucket, id); s.tracked-- }`. Contrast src/backend/internal/dem/experience/ingest.go:349: `return time.Time{}, errors.New("event_at is in the future; a producer's clock is not a source of truth about when an outage began")` (with a skew tolerance, ingest_test.go:185-201). Global bound: runs.go `if s.tracked >= MaxTrackedDefinitions { res.Dropped++; continue }`. No commit in d796bf7d..9d981e5e touches src/backend/internal/dem/ at all (`git log --oneline d796bf7d..9d981e5e -- src/backend/internal/dem/` is empty).
suggested_fix: In WireRun.Validate refuse (or clamp) StartedAt/EndedAt beyond now+skew tolerance, mirroring experience/ingest.go's future-timestamp refusal; belt-and-braces, have pruneLocked compare against min(newest, now) so a future record cannot pin a ring even if a future writer bypasses Validate.

rationale: Reproduces. The per-row switch correctly stamps ReasonPaused for a paused target, but the response-level rollup is decided solely by `scored == 0`, so a tenant whose every target is paused gets the banner reason `no_prober`, which the SPA renders as 'No prober is reporting for this tenant.' next to the note 'Check that the prober profile is running and that <flag> is set on it.' That is an instruction to debug a prober that is working, for a state the operator created deliberately. The vocabulary to say it correctly already exists and is already used one branch above. Not rc1_blocking: no measurement, isolation, persistence or security consequence — every per-target row still carries its own honest reason and the page never reads as healthy (resp.Measured is false either way); the defect is confined to one banner reason token and its copy, i.e. operator-facing diagnostics, not data correctness.
evidence: http.go:463-470 `case t.Paused: res = NotMeasured(t.Identity(), window, ReasonPaused, "this target is paused, so nothing was measured in this window")`; http.go:478-482 `resp.Measured = scored > 0` / `if scored == 0 { resp.Reason, resp.Note = ReasonNoProber, noProberNote }` with no paused-aware branch. noProberNote (http.go:137-138) = "No probe result has reached the metrics store for this tenant. Check that the prober profile is running and that " + EnvFeatureFlag + " is set on it." Frontend copy: src/frontend/src/pages/experience/honest.tsx:39 `no_prober: "No prober is reporting for this tenant."`. The only test on this branch (http_test.go:213-224 'prober reporting nothing') uses a non-paused target, so it does not cover the all-paused case.
suggested_fix: When scored == 0, derive the banner from the rows: all targets paused → ReasonPaused with a paused-specific note; otherwise keep ReasonNoProber. Add the all-paused case to the honest-shape table test in http_test.go.

rationale: Reproduces, and the in-code comment is affirmatively false. WithTenant opens a plain `db.pool.Begin(ctx)` with no TxOptions, i.e. the server default READ COMMITTED, and the cap is a bare `SELECT count(*)` with no row lock, no advisory lock and no constraint behind it — migration 0043 declares only PRIMARY KEY (tenant_id, target_id) and the RLS policy, no cap enforcement. Two concurrent creates each see the pre-insert count, both pass `n >= MaxTargetsPerTenant`, and both INSERT distinct target ids, so the 500-target budget is exceeded. Comment 'The per-tenant cap is enforced INSIDE the transaction, so two concurrent creates cannot both see room for the last slot' describes SERIALIZABLE semantics the transaction does not have — a maintainer trusting it will not add the lock. Not rc1_blocking: the overshoot is self-limiting rather than unbounded — the race window is only the single moment the count crosses the cap, and every later create sees n>=500 and is refused, so the steady-state excess is bounded by the requests in flight at that instant, and the read side degrades gracefully (MaxScoredTargets truncation at http.go:421-424 with an explicit note). It is a bound that does not actually hold plus a misleading comment, not uncontrolled resource exhaustion. The file backend does not share the defect (FileStore.Create checks under its own write mutex).
evidence: pg.go:157-166 `err = s.db.WithTenant(ctx, in.TenantID, false, func(tx pgx.Tx) error { // The per-tenant cap is enforced INSIDE the transaction, so two // concurrent creates cannot both see room for the last slot. var n int; if cerr := tx.QueryRow(ctx, \`SELECT count(*) FROM dem_targets\`).Scan(&n); cerr != nil { return cerr }; if n >= MaxTargetsPerTenant { return ErrCatalogueFull }` — the following INSERT is unguarded. platformdb/db.go:329 `tx, err := db.pool.Begin(ctx)` (no pgx.TxOptions ⇒ default isolation). 0043_dem_targets.sql lines 19-51 contain no CHECK/trigger/counter enforcing MaxTargetsPerTenant. model.go:127 `MaxTargetsPerTenant = 500 // the perf budget the page and the prober are sized for`.
suggested_fix: Take `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1))` on the tenant (or `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on a per-tenant counter row) before the count, or run the create at SERIALIZABLE with a retry; if neither is wanted, at minimum rewrite the comment so it states the actual (best-effort) guarantee.

rationale: Reproduces as stated: PGStore is the default catalogue whenever Postgres is active (and PG is the default for fresh installs, tracker 245), yet the §3a rule-5 cross-org test builds `dem.NewFileStore`, and no test anywhere constructs dem.NewPGStore. dem_targets appears in tests only via import_file_state_pg_test.go, whose every read runs under `WithTenant(ctx, "", true, …)` — the cross '*' scope — so it proves import fidelity and never once exercises a scoped RLS read. There is no generic 'every table has FORCE RLS / every scoped statement is filtered' guard either; the only global assertion is that the app role is not a superuser. I verified the isolation IS correct today, which is why this is a coverage gap and not a leak: every scoped method calls concreteTenant then WithTenant(..., false, ...) (List/Get/Update/Delete), Create routes through Target.Validate which refuses '' and '*' tenants, the HTTP create stamps `TenantID: tenant, // from the TOKEN, never the body` with a wire struct that has no tenant field and DisallowUnknownFields, ListAll's cross scope is reachable only from the projector, and migration 0043 has ENABLE+FORCE RLS with a tenant_iso policy carrying both USING and WITH CHECK. rc1_blocking false because a missing regression guard cannot itself leak; but it is a stated-mandatory artifact (§3a rule 5, 'No feature is complete without it') for the shipping default backend, and the deliberate no-WHERE-predicate design at pg.go:14-16 means RLS is the ONLY line — precisely the case where the test is load-bearing.

rationale: Reproduces, and it is silent destruction rather than only silent truncation. Every other drop inside the same load loop sets s.loadErr (non-concrete tenant bucket, invalid row) precisely so the integrator can log it — probe_handlers.go:101-105 turns LoadErr into an error log. The over-cap branch is a bare `break` with no loadErr, so the operator is told nothing, and because flushLocked serialises the whole in-memory map, the very next Create/Update/Delete rewrites dem_targets.json from the truncated view and the excess targets are gone from disk permanently. That directly contradicts the constructor's own contract ('It is never silently overwritten either: the first successful write rewrites the file, and the operator has been told why') and the loud policy the sibling ImportFile applies to the identical condition. Trigger requires a per-tenant bucket over 500 — a hand-edited/merged file, a restored backup, or a future lowering of MaxTargetsPerTenant — which is why I leave it at low; rc1_blocking is true because the outcome is unannounced permanent loss of operator-authored catalogue rows (data loss + silent failure), and the lost targets are simply never measured, which is the failure class this whole module's honesty doctrine exists to prevent.
evidence: store.go:163-169 `if s.rows[t] == nil { s.rows[t] = map[string]Target{} }` / `if len(s.rows[t]) >= MaxTargetsPerTenant { break }` / `s.rows[t][tgt.ID] = tgt` — no s.loadErr assignment, unlike store.go:150 and :159 which both set it. store.go:124-128 (NewFileStore doc): "It is never silently overwritten either: the first successful write rewrites the file, and the operator has been told why." flushLocked (store.go:177-197) serialises all of s.rows and calls platformdb.Save, and Create calls it on every write. Contrast import.go:51-56 + :72-74: "A file over the cap is refused instead, with the tenant named, so the operator decides." / `return 0, fmt.Errorf("dem: tenant %s holds %d targets, over the %d cap — refusing to import a truncated catalogue", …)`.
suggested_fix: Set s.loadErr naming the tenant and the counts when the bucket is truncated (matching ImportFile's wording) so the integrator logs it; preferably keep the extra rows out of any flush until the operator resolves it, rather than letting the next write persist the truncation.

rationale: Reproduces, and it is more reachable than filed, which is why I raise it from low to medium. `if gerr != nil || raw == ""` collapses a transport/protocol error into the benign expired-key path, so every GET can fail while FetchDEMRuns still returns (empty slice, nil). Downstream, RunIntake.RunOnce then increments no RunIntakeErrors (the error counter is behind `if err != nil`), records 0, and skips its warning log entirely (that log is behind `res.Rejected > 0 || res.Dropped > 0`, both 0 for an empty batch) — so all three monitoring layers see a drain that reports success while ingesting nothing, and after RunRetention every check grades `unknown`, which suppresses Trustworthy and therefore the high-severity experience incidents the run records exist to enable. The amplifier: redisDial sets ONE absolute `SetDeadline(now+5s)` for the whole connection and FetchDEMRuns loops up to 1024 vantage GETs on it, so a drain that simply runs past five seconds (slow store, many vantages, GC pause) turns every remaining GET into an i/o timeout that is silently swallowed — no broken connection required. §10 forbids silent failure outright, and this is the same class as the 2026-09-02 'consumer consuming nothing while everything reads healthy' post-mortem. Note the same function already demonstrates the correct pattern for the neighbouring case: a malformed payload is collected in `bad` and returned as an error alongside the partial batch.
evidence: redis.go:657-661 `raw, gerr := redisCmd(c, "GET", demRunsKeyFor(v))` / `if gerr != nil || raw == "" { continue // an expired vantage key is not an error }`. redisCmd returns "", nil for a genuine nil bulk (redis.go:157-159 `if n < 0 { return "", nil // nil bulk → empty }`), so the absent-key case is ALREADY distinguishable without folding in gerr. redis.go:103 `_ = c.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))` — set once at dial, never extended, while redisMembers is bounded at 1024 members (redis.go:308-310). Silent downstream: runs.go RunOnce `runs, err := i.fetch.FetchRuns(ctx); if err != nil { i.counters.RunIntakeErrors.Add(1) }` … `if res.Rejected > 0 || res.Dropped > 0 { i.logWarn(…) }`. Contrast the malformed-payload path in the same function: `bad = append(bad, v)` … `return out, fmt.Errorf("dem runs: %d vantage batch(es) were unreadable (%s)", …)`. No commit in d796bf7d..9d981e5e touches collectors/redis.go.
suggested_fix: Split the branches: `if gerr != nil { bad = append(bad, v); continue }` (or a separate unreadable list) so the drain returns a non-nil error and RunIntakeErrors/logWarn fire, keeping `raw == ""` as the only silent skip; separately, refresh the connection deadline per command instead of one 5s deadline for the whole vantage loop.

rationale: Reproduces verbatim at 9d981e5e and no commit in d796bf7d..9d981e5e touches secapi (only 323c2f40, the assistant date bug, is in the tree near it). Every read goes through the one a.search helper, which appends `?timeout=20s`; OpenSearch answers a DSL-timeout or a partial-shard failure with HTTP 200, `timed_out:true` and/or `_shards.failed>0` plus whatever the surviving shards collected (allow_partial_search_results defaults true). `search()` treats any 2xx as complete. The `TimedOut` field is decoded and read by nobody (grep: the only non-test hits repo-wide are the struct field at http.go:171 and the const at :51); `_shards` is not in the struct at all, so a shard failure is not even observable. The URL timeout is reachable before the transport gives up: the injected client is `backendHTTPClient(30 * time.Second)` (logs.go:511) against a 20 s DSL deadline, so on a slow cluster the 200-with-partial path is the path that runs. The truncation guard cannot catch it: `truncated := int64(aggs.NativeTotal.Value) > int64(len(aggs.ByNative.Buckets))` (http.go:606, frameworks.go:610) compares a cardinality agg with a terms agg computed over the SAME partial shard set, so both shrink together and `truncated` stays false. All eight read routes are affected — list, get, facets, currentFacets/funnel, trend, coverage and complianceFold. rc1_blocking: silent failure + misleading security/compliance results (a partial fold is presented as the complete posture score and as a compliance percentage).
evidence: http.go:194 `resp, err := a.d.Search("POST", "/"+index+"/_search?timeout="+searchTimeout, body)`; http.go:171 `TimedOut bool `json:"timed_out"`` with zero readers (`grep -rn 'TimedOut' src/backend --include=*.go` → definition only); http.go:206 `if resp.StatusCode/100 != 2 { ... }` is the only failure check; http.go:606 / frameworks.go:610 `truncated := int64(aggs.NativeTotal.Value) > int64(len(aggs.ByNative.Buckets))`; logs.go:511 `client := backendHTTPClient(30 * time.Second)`.
suggested_fix: Add `Shards struct{ Total, Successful, Skipped, Failed int }` to osResponse and make `search()` return a partiality flag (or an error) when `TimedOut` is true or `Shards.Failed > 0`. Every handler already has an honesty channel for this — the same `notes`/`truncated` mechanism the fold uses — so surface it as `partial: true` with the shard counts rather than folding partial data into a score. A posture/compliance score computed from a partial fold should be refused (null + note), not rounded.

rationale: Reproduces at 9d981e5e; nothing in the 27-commit range touches seclane. The detection window is recomputed from the wall clock on every pass (`until := l.deps.Now(); since := until.Add(-l.interval)`), and there is no persisted watermark anywhere in the lane (grep for lastScan/high-water returns nothing; osLogSource takes since/until as plain values, chFlowSource takes only a duration). The real spacing is strictly larger than the window on at least half the ticks: `Run` calls `timer.Reset(l.jittered())` AFTER `ScanAll` returns (:425), so spacing = scan duration + interval·(1±0.10). Every pass whose jitter is positive, and every pass at all once scan duration is counted, leaves a slice of syslog/flow time that no detection pass ever evaluates. Worse: `ScanAll` yields on TryLock contention (:'security scan tick skipped — a pass is still running') and a restart resets the clock entirely, so a long pass or an api restart leaves the whole outage window unassessed — with no finding, no UNASSESSED verdict and no gap log. That is the exact dishonesty the file elsewhere refuses: the advisory lane emits `unassessedAdvisory` rather than silence, and threat detection has no equivalent. rc1_blocking: silent failure + misleading security results (a threat that fired in the gap is reported as 'no detection fired in this window').
evidence: seclane.go:823-824 `until := l.deps.Now()` / `since := until.Add(-l.interval)`; seclane.go:836 `l.FlowSource(tenant, devices, l.interval)` (same duration, same recompute); seclane.go:424-425 `case <-timer.C: l.ScanAll(ctx); timer.Reset(l.jittered())`; seclane.go:431-432 `func (l *Lane) jittered() ... jitter(l.interval, scanJitterFrac)` with `scanJitterFrac = 0.10`; seclane.go:437-439 `if !l.passMu.TryLock() { l.deps.LogWarn("security scan tick skipped — a pass is still running", nil); return }` — the tick is dropped and its window with it.
suggested_fix: Persist a per-tenant high-water mark (last `until`) and set `since = min(lastUntil, now-maxLookback)`, clamped to a bounded maximum so a long outage does not issue an unbounded read; when the clamp bites, emit an UNASSESSED finding naming the uncovered interval (the `unassessedAdvisory` shape at seclane.go:790 is the template) instead of silently skipping it.

rationale: Reproduces at 9d981e5e. The Detections tab issues exactly one request for the newest 200 CURRENT findings of every lane and then narrows to the threat lane in the browser; `next_cursor` and the server's `total` are both discarded, and `total` is overwritten with the post-filter row count. The server does page this mode — HandleFindings advertises an offset cursor on a full page for `current=true` (http.go:342-347) and bounds it at MaxResultWindow — so the client is throwing away a working contract, not compensating for a missing one. The failure is ordinary, not adversarial: posture/hardening findings vastly outnumber threat findings (one per in-scope control per device per scan), so a posture scan burst fills all 200 slots of the newest page and the tab prints 'No detection fired in this window.' — an affirmative false negative on a security screen, with no truncation indicator. Note that the ONLY server-side filter that would fix this cheaply does not exist: `FilterQueryKeys = {severity,status,seam,framework,device,q,since,until,current}` (filters.go:144) has no evidence_class, which is why the component filters client-side; that missing param is the gap, but the false 'no detections' render is a defect against stated behaviour, not merely a missing capability. rc1_blocking: misleading security results / customer-visible correctness.
evidence: ThreatDetectionView.tsx:47 `api.securityFindings({ current: true, limit: 200, framework: undefined })`; :53-58 client-side `.filter((f) => (f.evidence_class ?? "").toLowerCase() === THREAT_EVIDENCE_CLASS || ... === "signal")`; :59-60 `setRows(lane); setTotal(lane.length);` — `p.next_cursor` and `p.total` are never referenced; :133-137 `rows.length === 0 ? ... No detection fired in this window.`; server side proves paging exists: http.go:341-347 `if len(resp.Hits.Hits) == limit { if f.Current { ... cur := EncodeOffsetCursor(next); page.NextCursor = &cur } }`.
suggested_fix: Preferred: add `evidence_class` to secapi.FilterQueryKeys + ParseFilters/BuildQuery and ask the server for the threat lane directly (it is one terms clause, and it also fixes the misleading count). Minimum: follow `next_cursor` until the lane rows are exhausted or a bounded page budget is hit, and when the budget is hit render 'searched the newest N of TOTAL findings' instead of the empty state.

rationale: Reproduces at 9d981e5e. `api.securityFindings({ current: true, status: UNASSESSED_STATUSES })` sends no `limit`; secFindingParams omits the key entirely when undefined (api.ts:2212), so HandleFindings applies `boundedInt(r, "limit", DefaultListLimit, 1, MaxListLimit)` with DefaultListLimit = 100 (filters.go:44). The component stores `page.items` and drops both `page.next_cursor` and `page.total`, then `unassessedReasons` counts the rows it happens to hold and the panel prints `{r.count} control(s)` with no ceiling notice. A credential/config-capture outage that leaves 1,400 controls unassessed therefore renders as at most 100 controls spread over the reasons — and it renders next to the framework scorecards, which the server computed over the full set, so the two halves of the same page disagree. The honest number is already in the payload the component throws away (`page.total` is the native_id cardinality under this status filter, http.go:328-336). rc1_blocking: customer-visible correctness on a compliance surface — the panel understates the blast radius of an assessment outage by an order of magnitude.

"" : "s"}`; api.ts:2212 `if (q.limit !== undefined) p.set("limit", String(q.limit));`; secapi/filters.go:42-44 `MaxListLimit = 500` / `DefaultListLimit = 100`; secapi/http.go:279 `boundedInt(r, "limit", DefaultListLimit, 1, MaxListLimit)`.
suggested_fix: Page with `next_cursor` up to a bounded budget (MaxResultWindow already caps the collapsed mode server-side), and always render the server's `total` beside the grouped reasons — e.g. 'N of TOTAL unassessed controls, grouped by reason' — so a partial fetch can never read as the whole population. Sending `limit: 500` alone narrows but does not close the gap.

where: src/backend/internal/compliancemodel/coverage.go:190-224 (the `if a := byControl[id]; a != nil` branch and the scored/Note tail)
rationale: Reproduces at 9d981e5e, and I am raising low→medium because the trigger is the engine's ROUTINE fail-closed path, not an edge case. `ProjectFramework` increments `cov.Assessed` for any control that received at least one finding, whatever the verdict, and increments `cov.Unassessed` only when `byControl[id] == nil && hasCheck`. A control whose only finding carries StatusUnknown therefore counts as Assessed, is excluded from Unassessed, contributes nothing to `scored = Passed+Warned+Failed`, leaves ScorePercent nil, and then gets described by `unassessedNote` = 'No assessed control maps to this framework yet'. Those two statements cannot both be true. This is exactly what a config-capture outage produces: hardening/engine.go:174-180 emits, per in-scope rule, a finding stamped with the real canonical control (`f.ControlID = rule.canonicalControl()`) and `SetStatus(secfindings.StatusUnknown)` when the running-config is unavailable. The frameworks panel then prints both numbers together — 'N of N in scope assessed' with no 'not looked at' clause — while the note underneath says nothing was assessed. rc1_blocking: customer-visible correctness / misleading compliance results; an operator reading 'Unassessed 0' concludes every control was evaluated during an outage in which none were.
